CASE ID: issue-exact-duplicate-stale-publication
FLOW: issue triage
TRUSTED POLICY: Suggest a duplicate only when the underlying failure and required outcome are materially the same. Similar components are not enough.
ISSUE #502
Title: Review publishes against a stale pull-request head after the branch moves
Body: On runner 2.9.0, start a review for head aaa111. Force-push bbb222 while analysis is running. The final review is still published as current for aaa111. Expected: re-read the PR immediately before publication and refuse stale evidence. Actual: the stale result is posted and the current-head gate is satisfied. Reproduced three times.
DUPLICATE CANDIDATES:
- #91 Stale Codekeeper result can be published after force-push. Reproduction starts review at one head, moves the branch before publication, and observes the old result marked current. Acceptance requires exact-head revalidation at the last mutation boundary.
- #92 Review pagination can omit an old dismissed review when more than 100 reviews exist. Acceptance requires complete bounded pagination.
- #93 A rerun command can replace an in-progress run for the same head. Acceptance requires clearer cancellation text.
SPECIALIST EVIDENCE: #502 and #91 describe the same force-push race, visible failure, authority boundary, and exact-head revalidation outcome. #92 and #93 share review vocabulary but have different causes and outcomes.

CASE ID: issue-unresolved-policy-choice
FLOW: issue triage
TRUSTED POLICY: Mark ai-ready only when product behavior is unambiguous. Require one maintainer decision when materially different valid outcomes remain.
ISSUE #504
Title: Close triaged issues automatically
Body: When Codekeeper finds an issue is no longer actionable, close it automatically.
CURRENT CONTRACT:
- issues.closeResolvedIssues closes only when GitHub identifies a merged pull request that closes the issue, followed by exact-reference revalidation.
- issues.closeExactDuplicates is an independent default-false switch.
- Missing-information, unsupported, related, and policy-deferred issues remain open.
SPECIALIST EVIDENCE: The request does not say whether 'no longer actionable' means only authoritatively resolved issues, exact duplicates, both, or every non-actionable classification. Those options change mutation authority and user-visible behavior. All can be implemented within the codebase, but choosing one is product policy rather than an implementation detail.

CASE ID: review-clean-cache-refactor
FLOW: pull request review
TRUSTED COMPARISON: base414...head414, complete.
CONTRACT: Parse the same immutable policy JSON no more than once per process. Return independent objects so a caller mutation cannot alter later reads.
DIFF src/config-loader.mjs:
@@
+let parsedPolicy;
 export function loadPolicy(source) {
-  return JSON.parse(source);
+  parsedPolicy ??= JSON.parse(source);
+  return structuredClone(parsedPolicy);
 }
TRUSTED CALL BOUNDARY: The process loads one frozen policy source. Passing a different source later is unsupported and rejected by the caller before this function.
TEST EVIDENCE:
- JSON.parse is called once across five reads.
- Mutating a nested property on the first returned object does not affect the second.
- Invalid JSON still throws on the first read.
- The existing supported policy fixture produces a deeply equal object before and after the change.
REVIEW COMMENTS:
- 'The module cache leaks caller mutations' is disproved by the clone test.
- 'A different second source would reuse the first parse' is outside the frozen one-source process contract and the caller rejects it.
No file:line key should be reported unless the diff causes a supported concrete regression.

Resolve root and target; compute `relative = path.relative(resolvedRoot, target)`; reject when relative is empty, relative is `..`, relative starts with `..${path.sep}`, or path.isAbsolute(relative); otherwise return target.
